_doc: Declared authority for every shortcode and block this plugin registers.
RenderSurfaceAuthorityTest walks the LIVE registries ($GLOBALS['shortcode_tags'] and
WP_Block_Type_Registry), keeps the entries whose callback/render.php lives inside this
plugin, and fails when one of them is missing here - so a new shortcode or block cannot
ship without someone stating whether it takes an object id.
id_att   - the attribute that names an object. Every renderer that has one is DISPATCHED
anonymously against a private fixture of every type (media, document, album,
collection) and must disclose nothing that belongs to it.
null     - takes no object id. MUST carry a reason saying why it cannot leak one.
user_att - takes a user id rather than an object id. Rendered anonymously scoped to the
fixture owner; the owner's private item must not appear.
discloses - fields this renderer reveals ON PURPOSE (title|slug). Requires a reason.
Everything else - file path, signed URL, description, the ids of items the
renderer discovered rather than was handed - is still checked.

mvs_lock_overlay.reason: The block IS the teaser for gated content: an editor places it naming one item so a visitor can be told what is behind the lock and offered a way in. The title and the login-redirect permalink are the product. The file, the signed URL and the thumbnail are not, and are still asserted absent. OPEN QUESTION for the owner: it teases items with no access rule and so no unlock path, where the teaser reveals a private title for nothing.

mvs_gallery.reason: A query, not an object: it renders through mvs/media-grid, whose SQL carries MediaRepository::explore_privacy_clause() for the current viewer.

mvs_member_photos.reason: A member's grid. Delegates to mvs/media-grid, so the same viewer-scoped privacy clause decides every row.

mvs_explore_feed.reason: The public feed. No id; rows come from the same viewer-scoped privacy clause.

mvs_documents.reason: Lists MediaRepository::public_documents() only - it never tries to answer 'what may this viewer see', it lists what is already public. The folder/drive branches hand off to Pro's permission ladder.

mvs_stats.reason: Aggregate counts for the whole site. Takes no id and names no item.

mvs_dashboard.reason: The signed-in member's own dashboard. Renders an auth gate for anonymous visitors.

mvs_profile_edit.reason: The signed-in member's own profile form. Returns a log-in prompt for anonymous visitors.

mvs_usage_history.reason: The signed-in member's own upload ledger. Returns '' for anonymous visitors.

mvs/lock-overlay.reason: Same renderer as [mvs_lock_overlay]; see the reason there.

mvs/media-grid.reason: The one grid emitter. Its SQL carries MediaRepository::explore_privacy_clause() for the current viewer, so the gate is in the query rather than in a per-row filter.
